questions.question: What is the primary purpose of descriptive statistics in psychological research?

answers.text: To summarize and display data from a sample
To determine causality between variables
To test hypotheses about population parameters
To randomly assign participants to conditions

questions.question: In a frequency table, the levels of a variable are typically ordered:

answers.text: From highest at the top to lowest at the bottom
Alphabetically from A to Z
Randomly to avoid bias
From lowest at the top to highest at the bottom

questions.question: A distribution with two distinct peaks is called:

answers.text: Bimodal
Unimodal
Negatively skewed
Symmetrical

questions.question: A negatively skewed distribution has:

answers.text: Its peak shifted toward the upper end with a long negative tail
Its peak shifted toward the lower end with a long positive tail
Two distinct peaks of equal height
A perfectly symmetrical shape

questions.question: The mean is calculated by:

answers.text: Summing all scores and dividing by the number of scores
Finding the middle score in an ordered distribution
Identifying the most frequently occurring score
Subtracting the lowest score from the highest score

questions.question: When there is an even number of scores, the median is:

answers.text: The value halfway between the two middle scores
The sum of the two middle scores
The lower of the two middle scores
The most frequently occurring score

questions.question: Which measure of central tendency is most appropriate for highly skewed distributions?

answers.text: Median
Mean
Mode
Range

questions.question: The range is calculated as:

answers.text: The difference between the highest and lowest scores
The average distance between scores and the mean
The square root of the variance
The sum of squared deviations from the mean

questions.question: The standard deviation represents:

answers.text: The average distance between the scores and the mean
The difference between the highest and lowest scores
The middle score in a distribution
The percentage of scores below a given value

questions.question: When computing the standard deviation, why do researchers often divide by N − 1 instead of N?

answers.text: To correct for the tendency of sample standard deviations to underestimate population standard deviations
To make the calculation easier and faster
To ensure the result is always a whole number
To eliminate outliers from the calculation

questions.question: A percentile rank of 80 means that:

answers.text: 80% of scores in the distribution are lower than that score
The score is 80% of the maximum possible score
80% of scores are higher than that score
The score is 80 points above the mean

questions.question: A z score of +0.67 indicates that a raw score is:

answers.text: 0.67 standard deviations above the mean
0.67 points above the mean
67% higher than the average score
0.67 standard deviations below the mean

questions.question: Outliers are sometimes defined as scores with z scores:

answers.text: Less than −3.00 or greater than +3.00
Less than −1.00 or greater than +1.00
Exactly equal to zero
Between −0.50 and +0.50

questions.question: Cohen's d is calculated by:

answers.text: Dividing the difference between two means by the standard deviation
Computing the mean cross-product of z scores
Subtracting the smallest mean from the largest mean
Dividing the variance by the sample size

questions.question: According to Cohen's guidelines, a Cohen's d value of 0.50 is considered:

answers.text: Medium
Small
Large
Trivial

questions.question: Pearson's r is described as:

answers.text: The mean cross-product of z scores
The difference between two group means
The percentage of variance explained
The sum of squared deviations

questions.question: According to Cohen's guidelines, a Pearson's r value of ±0.10 is considered:

answers.text: Small/weak
Medium
Strong/large
Perfect correlation

questions.question: In APA style, numerical results should be rounded to:

answers.text: Two decimal places
One decimal place
The nearest whole number
Three decimal places

questions.question: Error bars in APA-style bar graphs most commonly represent:

answers.text: One standard error in each direction
The full range of scores
The median value
The mode of the distribution

questions.question: A planned analysis is one that:

answers.text: Tests a relationship that was expected based on a hypothesis
Explores data for unexpected patterns without a prior hypothesis
Excludes all outliers before examining the data
Is conducted only after inferential statistics are complete
